responses.reason: The arithmetic in this challenge is wrong. $186,000 less $121,000 is $65,000, not $6,500, and $65,000 on $186,000 is 34.9 percent, not 3.5 percent. Both legs of the threshold pass, the table itself stars the line, and commentary is owed on it rather than excused.

S1 says the roof and dock leveler program finished on June 30 and S10 says the remaining depot repairs finish in August. I believe S10 because it admits spend still to come, and it matters because the close needs to know whether an accrual for committed work is missing from the $77,600.

The table shows $214,000 going to $287,800, an increase of $73,800 and 34.5 percent, so the account rose. S6 says it declined, which reverses the sign, and easing carrier surcharges cannot be the driver of a 34.5 percent increase in freight cost.

The plans were billed in June and cover the twelve months to May 2027, so only one month, $7,000, is June revenue. The entry should have credited deferred revenue for $77,000, and that $77,000 is a third of the $229,000 movement the memo calls growth.

Professional fees moved $7,500, which fails the $25,000 leg outright, so no commentary and no supporting evidence are owed on this line. The memo already says so in S12, and holding the release for an engagement letter on an immaterial movement is the wrong use of the close calendar.

Inventory shrink moved $2,500, which is 39.1 percent but nowhere near the $25,000 leg, so it fails the threshold that requires both. The table does not star it, no commentary is owed, and I would not hold a memo release for a cycle count file on $2,500.

I have seen no support for the Tri-State ramp, and S4 credits demand across all four depots for the same $372,000, so the memo offers two drivers that contradict each other. I would want the revenue by depot for both months and the customer count behind the ramp before release.

The account moved $15,000 to $62,000, which is $47,000, and S2 says $42,000. The $5,000 difference is unexplained, so either the Coastal Grocers reserve is being misquoted or there is a second reserve movement nobody has named.

The invoices are for June fuel, so they belong in June and should have been accrued at close, debit fleet fuel and credit accrued liabilities for $19,400. Recorded properly the line goes from a $5,200 decline to a $14,200 increase, which is the opposite story.

Software subscriptions moved $1,600 and 5.6 percent, failing both legs, so S3 should not be in the memo at all. It is the most detailed sentence written, down to prorated seats, and it displaced warehouse wages at $72,500 and freight billed at $65,000, both of which pass and both of which got nothing.

Warehouse wages moved $72,500 on $630,000, which is 11.5 percent, so both legs pass and a driver is required. I would ask for headcount by depot, overtime hours and the rate change with its effective date, because at that size it is either volume, overtime or a rate move and the memo names none of them.

Freight billed fell $65,000 while product revenue rose $372,000, which is the pattern you see when a distributor moves to delivered pricing and rolls freight into the product price. Neither sentence discloses that, so I would test the $65,000 as a transfer and treat only the remaining $307,000 as real growth.

Recomputed unrounded, May margin is 1,310,000 on 5,240,000 or 25.00 percent and June is 1,334,000 on 5,612,000 or 23.77 percent. That is 123 basis points of compression, so the claim of 24 percent in both months is wrong and mix and pricing were not stable.

The driver offered is depot equipment additions sitting in depreciation, but account 7000 moved zero dollars over the month, so the additions are not in these numbers at all. A 51 percent rise in interest with flat depreciation reads as revolver borrowing, and the $31,200 is left unexplained.

findings: Account 6200 repairs and maintenance: a roof replacement and dock levelers are capital work, not repairs expense. The $77,600 at 189.3 percent should be tested against the capitalisation policy, and the challenge list raised only the timing contradiction, not the classification.

Account 4200 freight billed to customers needs a driver of its own regardless of any transfer to product revenue. It fell $65,000 and 34.9 percent, it is starred, and no sentence in the memo mentions it, while account 5100 inbound freight rose 34.5 percent in the same month.
